verified.title: On Cost-Effective LLM-as-a-Judge Improvement Techniques
verified.authors_or_org: Ryan Lail, Luke Markham
verified.mechanism: Compares ensemble scoring, criteria injection, calibration context, and adaptive escalation; ensemble+criteria injection reach 85.8% accuracy (+13.5pp over baseline), generalizing across providers.
verified.design_lesson: Combine ensemble scoring with per-task criteria injection in RQGM's held-out judge to cut scalar-score noise; reserve costly escalation only for low-confidence verdicts.
verified.token_lesson: Use adaptive escalation: cheap single-pass judging by default, expensive re-scoring only when judge confidence is low.

verified.title: Efficient Inference for Noisy LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation
verified.authors_or_org: Yiqun T Chen, Sizhu Lu, Sijia Li, Moran Guo, Shengyi Li
verified.mechanism: Derives efficient estimators via semiparametric theory, comparing measurement-error correction vs. prediction-powered inference to debias noisy judge outputs without extra full judge calls.
verified.design_lesson: Statistically debias RQGM's held-out judge scores via PPI-style correction instead of paying for repeated full-context re-judging each iteration.
verified.token_lesson: Correct noisy judge scores post hoc with prediction-powered inference rather than re-running full judge calls.

verified.title: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
verified.authors_or_org: Hangfan Zhang, Shao Zhang, Kangcong Li, Chen Zhang, Yang Chen, Yiqun Zhang, Lei Bai, Shuyue Hu
verified.mechanism: Agents autonomously refine their own harnesses via failure-pattern identification, targeted modification generation, and regression-test validation, yielding up to 132% relative gains.
verified.design_lesson: Let RQGM's meta-loop autonomously edit its own harness/prompt using failure-pattern diagnosis plus regression-test validation before adopting each mutation.

verified.title: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses
verified.authors_or_org: Jiahang Lin, Shichun Liu, Chengjun Pan, Lizhi Lin, Shihan Dou, Zhiheng Xi, Xuanjing Huang, Hang Yan, Zhenhua Han, Tao Gui, Yu-Gang Jiang
verified.mechanism: Three observability pillars—editable/revertible harness components, trajectory-to-evidence conversion, prediction-verified edits—lift Terminal-Bench 2 pass rate 69.7% to 77.0%, transferring across benchmarks.
verified.design_lesson: Require every RQGM loop-design edit to be revertible, backed by trajectory evidence, and validated against a stated prediction before merging into the next epoch.

verified.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
verified.authors_or_org: Yike Wang, Huaisheng Zhu, Zhengyu Hu, Yige Yuan, Zhengyu Chen, Shakti Senthil, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Yulia Tsvetkov, Pradeep Dasigi, Teng Xiao
verified.mechanism: Matched-budget ablation shows harness-evolution evaluations conflate design gains with extra search budget; evolution often underperforms simple test-time scaling and generalizes poorly to held-out tasks.
verified.design_lesson: Ablate each RQGM loop-design mutation against a matched-compute baseline (more sampling, same budget) before crediting the loop-design change itself.

verified.title: DemoEvolve: Overcoming Sparse Feedback in Agentic Harness Evolution with Demonstrations
verified.authors_or_org: Lirong Che, Yuzhe Yang, Peiwen Lin, Chuang Wang, Xueqian Wang, Jian Su
verified.mechanism: Injects human expert trajectories to guide harness editing under sparse, stochastic feedback, making evolution more diagnosable, localizable, and stable than self-rollout-only approaches.
verified.design_lesson: When RQGM's per-iteration feedback is sparse or noisy, seed mutations with a few human-approved exemplar trajectories instead of relying solely on self-generated rollouts.

verified.title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
verified.authors_or_org: Lakshya A Agrawal et al. (Berkeley/Stanford-affiliated)
verified.mechanism: Reflects in natural language on sampled trajectories to diagnose failures, mutates prompts, and maintains a Pareto archive of complementary variants; beats GRPO by 6% with far fewer rollouts.
verified.design_lesson: Replace RQGM's single-branch mutation lineage with a Pareto archive of complementary variants plus per-criterion textual reflection, not one scalar reward.
verified.token_lesson: Natural-language reflection on trajectories can replace costly RL rollouts while improving prompt quality.

verified.title: Autorubric: A Unifying Framework for Rubric-Based LLM Evaluation on Non-Verifiable Tasks
verified.authors_or_org: Delip Rao, Chris Callison-Burch
verified.mechanism: Unified API for rubric evaluation with configurable bias mitigation, calibration, ensembling, and abstention; reveals criterion-specific failures and judge-family differences across tasks.
verified.design_lesson: Give RQGM's held-out judge per-criterion isolated scoring calls with built-in abstention and calibration, exposing which specific criteria fail instead of one scalar score.

verified.title: Rethinking Rubric Generation for Improving LLM Judge and Reward Modeling for Open-ended Tasks
verified.authors_or_org: William F. Shen, Xinchi Qiu, Chenxi Whitehouse, Lisa Alazraki, Shashwat Goel, Francesco Barbieri, Timon Willi, Akhil Mathur, Ilias Leontiadis
verified.mechanism: RRD framework recursively decomposes and filters rubrics to remove overlap/redundancy, improving judge accuracy up to +17.7 points and reward-signal quality up to 160%.
verified.design_lesson: Periodically recursively decompose and de-duplicate RQGM's rubric criteria each epoch, rather than only re-scoring the artifact against a static rubric.

verified.title: SePO: Self-Evolving Prompt Agent for System Prompt Optimization
verified.authors_or_org: Wangcheng Tao, Han Wu, Weng-Fai Wong
verified.mechanism: A single self-referential agent optimizes both task-agent prompts and its own prompt via evolutionary search, pretrained across tasks then fine-tuned; beats Manual-CoT/TextGrad/MetaSPO by 4.49 pts avg.
verified.design_lesson: Make RQGM's own meta-prompt a first-class evolutionary target alongside the artifact, kept in a stepping-stone archive to prevent net-shrink regressions across epochs.

verified.title: Escher-Loop: Mutual Evolution by Closed-Loop Self-Referential Optimization
verified.authors_or_org: Ziyang Liu, Xinyan Guo, Xuchen Wei, Han Hao, Liu Yang
verified.mechanism: Coevolves Task Agents and Optimizer Agents; a dynamic benchmarking mechanism reuses task-agent scores to evaluate optimizers for free, surpassing static-baseline performance ceilings.
verified.design_lesson: Reuse RQGM's existing per-iteration scores to cheaply evaluate loop-design mutations themselves, avoiding a separate costly meta-evaluation pass each epoch.
verified.token_lesson: Score loop-design mutations by reusing existing per-iteration judge outputs instead of running a separate meta-eval pass.

verified.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge: Concerning Rubric Artifacts in LLM-based Automated Text Generation Evaluation
verified.authors_or_org: Anshul Bagaria, Sowmya S Sundaram, Gokul S Krishnan, Balaraman Ravindran
verified.mechanism: Classifiers trained only on rubric text (no responses) predict judge scores above chance, and judges often fail to flip scores when responses/criteria are intentionally reversed.
verified.design_lesson: Before adopting a rubric revision, test it with a rubric-only classifier and a reversed-response probe to catch artifact bias that would mask real stalls.

verified.title: Noise-Response Calibration: A Causal Intervention Protocol for LLM-Judges
verified.authors_or_org: Maxim Khomiakov, Jes Frellsen
verified.mechanism: Injects controlled input perturbations and measures causal response deltas; text-judges degrade predictably under noise while tabular judges do not, correlating noise-robustness with accuracy.
verified.design_lesson: Calibrate RQGM's held-out judge's noise floor via controlled perturbation probes each epoch rather than assuming a fixed noise-tolerance threshold.

verified.title: Noisy but Valid: Robust Statistical Evaluation of LLMs with Imperfect Judges
verified.authors_or_org: Chen Feng, Minghe Shen, Ananth Balashankar, Carsten Gerner-Beuerle, Miguel R. D. Rodrigues
verified.mechanism: Hypothesis-testing framework uses a calibration set to estimate judge TPR/FPR, giving finite-sample Type-I error control for pass/fail decisions despite imperfect judges.
verified.design_lesson: Define RQGM's 'gain pays for growth' pass/fail threshold via a calibrated hypothesis test with error control, not an ad hoc noise-adjusted cutoff.

verified.title: Measuring all the noises of LLM Evals
verified.authors_or_org: Sida Wang
verified.mechanism: Decomposes eval noise into prediction noise (model variance) and data noise (item sampling); prediction noise typically exceeds data noise and totals are highly predictable per eval.
verified.design_lesson: When RQGM stalls, first diagnose whether it's judge prediction noise or criterion/item sampling noise, since averaging judge calls usually helps more than adding criteria.

verified.title: When Judgment Becomes Noise: How Design Failures in LLM Judge Benchmarks Silently Undermine Validity
verified.authors_or_org: Benjamin Feuer, Chiung-Yi Tseng, Astitwa Sarthak Lathe, Oussama Elachqar, John P Dickerson
verified.mechanism: Schematic adherence and psychometric validity diagnostics show Arena-Hard-Auto rankings hide over 90% unexplained variance for some models, with aggregation masking true uncertainty.
verified.design_lesson: Replace RQGM's single aggregated score with structured per-criterion verdicts plus a psychometric-validity check so aggregation stops hiding real per-criterion progress.

verified.title: SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
verified.authors_or_org: Bingchen Zhao, Dhruv Srikanth, Yuxiang Wu, Zhengyao Jiang
verified.mechanism: Benchmarks reward hacking by comparing visible-test vs. held-out-test pass rates across 30 systems tasks; the gap grows 28pp per tenfold increase in code size.
verified.design_lesson: Have RQGM's held-out judge specifically probe for architectural shortcuts via held-out integration checks scaled to artifact size, not just surface criteria.

verified.title: Safety in Self-Evolving LLM Agent Systems: Threats, Amplification, and Case Studies
verified.authors_or_org: Ruixiao Lin, Xinhao Deng, Qingming Li, Jianan Ma, Yunhao Feng, Yuqi Qing, Zhenyuan Li, Yechao Zhang, Shiwen Cui, Changhua Meng, Tianwei Zhang, Xingjun Ma, Qi Li, Ke Xu, Shouling Ji
verified.mechanism: A Module-Lifecycle Attack Surface matrix finds self-evolving systems expose 3.5x more attack surface with 100% malicious-payload persistence, and existing defenses block only 2.5% of attacks.
verified.design_lesson: Bound how much a single RQGM epoch may change evaluator/judge weighting per step, since self-evolving loops let small evaluator flaws persist and compound.

verified.title: LLM-as-Judge on a Budget
verified.authors_or_org: Aadirupa Saha, Aniket Wagde, Branislav Kveton
verified.mechanism: Variance-adaptive multi-armed-bandit allocation directs repeated judge queries toward higher-uncertainty candidates/criteria instead of uniform re-scoring, with theoretical error bounds.
verified.design_lesson: Allocate RQGM's judge-call budget via a bandit targeting high-variance criteria for re-scoring, replacing the flat 3-full-context-judge pass to cut tokens.
verified.token_lesson: A variance-adaptive bandit over judge queries beats uniform re-scoring at the same query budget.

verified.title: Knockout LLM Assessment: Using Large Language Models for Evaluations through Iterative Pairwise Comparisons
verified.authors_or_org: Isik Baran Sandan, Tu Anh Dinh, Jan Niehues
verified.mechanism: Tournament-style single-elimination pairwise comparisons replace absolute scoring, improving correlation with human ratings by about 0.07 on exam and translation evaluation tasks.
verified.design_lesson: Consider pairwise knockout rounds between candidate variants instead of RQGM's absolute scalar score, cutting scoring noise with fewer full judge calls than round-robin.

verified.title: SCOPE: Selective Conformal Optimized Pairwise LLM Judging
verified.authors_or_org: Sher Badshah, Ali Emami, Hassan Sajjad
verified.mechanism: Conformal calibration sets an abstention threshold bounding error among non-abstained pairwise judgments at level alpha, using Bidirectional Preference Entropy as a bias-neutral uncertainty signal.
verified.design_lesson: Use conformal-calibrated abstention so RQGM re-judges only comparisons flagged uncertain, bounding error statistically while skipping confident ones to save tokens.
verified.token_lesson: Abstain-and-skip confident pairwise judgments via conformal calibration to cut redundant judge calls.

verified.title: Generating and Refining Dynamic Evaluation Rubrics for LLM-as-a-Judge
verified.authors_or_org: Zijie Wang, Eduardo Blanco
verified.mechanism: Training-free method generates dataset- and instance-level rubrics without human annotation, then iteratively refines them via meta-judge reward signals, outperforming larger proprietary baselines.
verified.design_lesson: Auto-generate and iteratively refine RQGM's per-iteration rubric at the instance level via meta-judge feedback instead of keeping one static rubric across epochs.

verified.title: Semantic Early-Stopping for Iterative LLM Agent Loops
verified.authors_or_org: Sahil Shrivastava
verified.mechanism: Halts writer-critic loops when consecutive draft embeddings stop changing meaning and quality plateaus, cutting tokens 38% vs. fixed iteration caps; quality-gated variants backfired on judging cost.
verified.design_lesson: Replace RQGM's fixed epoch cap with embedding-based plateau detection to auto-halt stalled epochs early; skip extra quality-gate judge calls, which raised cost without benefit.
verified.token_lesson: Semantic plateau detection on draft embeddings cut agent-loop tokens 38% versus fixed iteration limits.
